```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(pollinatoR)
```

## The design

Variety trials are often laid out as split plots. Each block holds one whole
plot per variety, and each whole plot is split in two: one half caged against
insects, the other left open. The pollination treatment is the sub-plot factor.
Two sources of error follow: whole plots differ from one another, and so do
sub-plots within a whole plot. The pollination contrast is read within whole
plots, where the variety and the patch of ground are shared.

The trial below is simulated: four blocks, eight canola varieties, and three
plants harvested from each sub-plot. Varieties differ both in yield and in how
much they depend on insects, and the two are unrelated.

```{r data}
set.seed(11)
n_block <- 4L
varieties <- sprintf("V%d", 1:8)
open_pods <- setNames(c(70, 95, 80, 110, 60, 90, 100, 75), varieties)
dependence <- c(0.10, 0.30, 0.20, 0.15, 0.35, 0.25, 0.05, 0.30)
names(dependence) <- varieties

trial <- expand.grid(
  plant = 1:3,
  trt = c("Cage", "Open"),
  variety = varieties,
  block = sprintf("B%d", seq_len(n_block)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
# Varieties are randomised to the whole plots of each block
whole_plot <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_block), function(b) sample(8L)))
blocks <- sprintf("B%d", seq_len(n_block))
names(whole_plot) <- paste(rep(blocks, each = 8L), varieties)
trial$plot <- sprintf("W%d", whole_plot[paste(trial$block, trial$variety)])

block_effect <- setNames(rnorm(n_block, 0, 0.10), blocks)
plot_effect <- setNames(rnorm(length(whole_plot), 0, 0.10), names(whole_plot))
cage <- trial$trt == "Cage"
mu <- open_pods[trial$variety] *
  ifelse(cage, 1 - dependence[trial$variety], 1) *
  exp(block_effect[trial$block] + plot_effect[paste(trial$block, trial$variety)])
trial$pods <- rnbinom(nrow(trial), mu = mu, size = 30)
head(trial)
```

## Data, design and estimand

The unit nesting is block, then whole plot. Variety is a grouping column: it
labels the whole plots but is not a level of the nesting.

```{r declare}
pd <- pollin_data(
  trial,
  response = "pods",
  treatment = "trt",
  unit = c("block", "plot"),
  groups = "variety"
)
ds <- pollin_design(
  pd,
  arms = c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"),
  layout = "split_plot"
)
ds
```

The `split_plot` layout gives each block and each whole plot its own random
intercept. The assumptions for this layout name the sub-plot randomisation.

```{r assumptions}
est <- pollin_estimand(ds, family = "dependence", scale = "ratio", basis = "loss")
knitr::kable(pollin_assumptions(est))
```

## The trial as a whole

Over all eight varieties, the dependence on the loss basis is the share of
open-plot yield lost under the cage. The same contrast on the gain basis is
the rise from caged to open plots. Both are given here, labelled, because they
are easily confused: the gain is always the larger of the two.

```{r overall}
loss <- pollin_effects(pollin_fit(est))
loss
est_gain <- pollin_estimand(ds, family = "dependence", scale = "ratio", basis = "gain")
gain <- pollin_effects(pollin_fit(est_gain))
gain$table[c("basis", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
```

## Dependence by variety

Breeders want the dependence of each variety. Giving `by = "variety"` to
`pollin_fit()` fits the treatment-by-variety interaction, so each variety has
its own fixed treatment effect, and `pollin_effects()` then reports one
contrast per variety.

```{r by-variety}
fit_v <- pollin_fit(est, by = "variety")
fit_v
by_variety <- pollin_effects(fit_v)$table
by_variety$planted <- dependence[by_variety$variety]
by_variety[c("variety", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "planted")]
```

Each variety's estimate rests on its own 24 plants, so the intervals are wide.
Seven of the eight intervals cover the planted value, about what 95% intervals
should give. A variety-by-variety reading needs more blocks than this.

On the difference scale the same fit gives pods per plant lost under the cage,
which mixes a variety's dependence with its yield.

```{r by-variety-difference}
est_diff <- pollin_estimand(
  ds,
  family = "dependence",
  scale = "difference",
  basis = "loss"
)
pollin_effects(pollin_fit(est_diff, by = "variety"))$table[
  c("variety", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")
]
```

## Guard: dependence against yield across varieties

A tempting next step is to regress each variety's dependence index on its open
yield, asking whether high-yielding varieties need insects more. When the index
is the RII and the yield axis is the open-plot yield, the open value sits on
both axes and part of any slope is built in. `pollin_guard_spurious()` permutes
the caged values across varieties, holding the open values fixed, to show the
slope that the shared term alone produces.

```{r spurious}
open_mean <- tapply(trial$pods[!cage], trial$variety[!cage], mean)
cage_mean <- tapply(trial$pods[cage], trial$variety[cage], mean)
pollin_guard_spurious(open_mean, cage_mean, n_perm = 500, seed = 1)
```

Eight varieties make a small panel, and the permutation null is wide. The
planted dependences were chosen independently of yield, and the guard does not
separate the observed slope from what the shared term would give.
